name: Project-Intelligence-Toolkit
summary: Project-Intelligence-Toolkit is a web application that tracks large capital projects (nuclear, LNG, wind, solar, oil and gas, grid, real estate and more) in a shared database called the Yard. It gathers evidence by searching the web, reading pages with AI models, and keeping only facts backed by an exact quote from a live source. On top of that data it offers several tools: Reality Scan (benchmarking budgets and delays), Lessons Learnt (themes behind success and trouble, exported as PowerPoint decks), and an Opportunity Map (spotting new project signals). A large set of scripts imports research batches, repairs data, and checks quality. How the pieces outside the API server fit in is unclear, because only the API server files were described.
who_its_for: Analysts, researchers and consultants who need source-backed benchmarks and slide decks about big infrastructure projects. Developers and data stewards who load and verify the research data also use it.
how_it_runs: The API server is a Node.js (Express) program that talks to a PostgreSQL database and AI and search services, and it is built into one file by artifacts/api-server/build.mjs. It is set up for Replit hosting (.replit) with settings copied from .env.example to .env. The website front end is not described, so how it is served is unclear beyond a static file server.

areas.name: artifacts
areas.summary: This holds the API server: web routes, login, the database layer, research jobs, evidence capture, search and AI model routing, plus the Reality Scan, Lessons Learnt and Opportunity Map tools. The script folder inside it holds many import, repair, audit and test scripts.
areas.why: It is where nearly all the real work of the product happens.
areas.debug_tips: Check the server logs and the health routes first, then the environment settings report. For bad data, run the read-only audit scripts and verify.ts before changing anything.

readiness.summary: Top fixes: add CI with a test script and a dependency audit, write a deploy and rollback procedure with database backup and restore, and scan git history for secrets while confirming auth and input checks on every route.

checks.question: Does the app build and start with one documented command?
checks.evidence: `README.md` documents a clear sequence (`pnpm install`, `pnpm run local:env`, `pnpm run db:schema`, `pnpm run db:seed`, `pnpm run dev`) with requirements listed, and `package.json` defines matching scripts. It is several commands rather than one, and the build was not run, so a working start is not confirmed.
checks.next_step: Add a single `pnpm run setup` wrapper for steps 2 to 4 and confirm a clean-machine start.

checks.question: Are there automated tests, and do they pass?
checks.evidence: Not checked: tests were not run in this pass. 26 test files exist (for example `artifacts/api-server/src/lib/money.test.ts`, `artifacts/api-server/src/evidence/evidenceRules.test.ts`), but no `test` script appears in the root `package.json` and there is no CI config.
checks.next_step: Add a root `test` script and run it in CI.

checks.question: When something goes wrong, does the app show a clear message instead of crashing or failing silently?
checks.evidence: Only 1 swallowed-error match was found across the repo, which is a good sign, and the README describes 'not configured' states for missing AI keys. No evidence was seen of a global error handler or user-facing error messages in the web app.
checks.next_step: Confirm an Express error middleware and a React error boundary exist, and fix the one swallowed error.

checks.question: Does it check what people type or upload before using it?
checks.evidence: Validation appears widespread (1634 matches in 285 files) and the repo has a shared `lib/api-zod` contract, which suggests schema-based request checks. Upload limits, file type checks and coverage on every route were not verified.
checks.next_step: Check that every route parses input with the zod schemas and that uploads have size and type limits.

checks.question: Are passwords and API keys kept out of the code and out of git history?
checks.evidence: `.gitignore` covers `.env`, only `.env.example` is tracked, and no secret-looking strings were found in HEAD. Git history was not scanned, and the JWT secret is generated locally by `pnpm run local:env`, which is good practice.
checks.next_step: Run a history scan (for example gitleaks) and rotate anything it finds.

checks.question: Can only the right people see and change things (sign-in and permissions)?
checks.evidence: Auth and permission code is widespread (868 matches in 200 files), and the README describes login with a JWT secret. There is an `AUTH_DISABLED` dev bypass that the README says is ignored in production builds, but that was not verified in code. Per-resource permission checks were not reviewed.
checks.next_step: Verify the production guard on `AUTH_DISABLED` and test that each route enforces roles.

checks.question: Is important data backed up, and are database changes made through migrations?
checks.evidence: Drizzle migrations exist in `lib/db/migrations`, with a schema snapshot `schema.sql`. However, `db:schema` is described as running only on an empty database, and no backup or restore procedure was found in the docs.
checks.next_step: Document scheduled database backups and a tested restore, and confirm how migrations are applied to existing databases.

checks.question: Are third-party packages reasonably up to date and free of known security problems?
checks.evidence: Not checked: the dependency audit was not run. Lockfiles `pnpm-lock.yaml` and `uv.lock` are committed, which helps reproducibility, and Python deps use minimum version pins.
checks.next_step: Run `pnpm audit` and a Python audit, and add automated dependency updates.

checks.question: If it breaks while people use it, will logs or alerts show what happened?
checks.evidence: Logging appears in 247 matches across 79 files, so some logging exists. No evidence of structured logging, request IDs, error tracking or alerting was seen.
checks.next_step: Add structured logging with request IDs and an error tracker or alert on 5xx rates.

checks.question: Does it stay fast with realistic amounts of data and users?
checks.evidence: Not checked: no load tests, pagination review or query analysis were available in the static evidence, and nothing was run.
checks.next_step: Review list endpoints for pagination and indexes, and run a basic load test against seeded data.

checks.question: Is there a written, repeatable way to deploy it and to roll back a bad release?
checks.evidence: No CI or deploy files were found, and the README covers local running only. There is no written deploy or rollback procedure.
checks.next_step: Write a `DEPLOY.md` covering build, migrate, release and rollback, and add a CI pipeline.

checks.question: Could someone new run it and understand it from the docs alone?
checks.evidence: `README.md` has a clear overview, repo layout table, requirements, step-by-step local setup, optional keys and `.env.example`. Further READMEs cover the tools and data directories, and `CLAUDE.md` is present.
checks.next_step: Add an architecture overview and a troubleshooting section.

readiness.method: Static evidence only; tests, build and audit were not run in this pass.

debug_playbook.symptom: The server will not start or features say a key is missing
steps: Open the health route to see which keys are set.
Run the model and search live checks to confirm the keys actually work.

debug_playbook.symptom: A project value or quote looks wrong or unsupported
steps: Use the value inspector route to see where the value came from.
Run the read-only quote audit to see whether the quote is found on its source page.
Check the evidence review hold scripts if the value was withheld.

debug_playbook.symptom: A research job fails or finds nothing
steps: Look at the job's saved step records to see which of the four steps failed.
Run the search diagnostic to check search results are usable links.
Confirm the search and model keys, including the backup keys, still work.

debug_playbook.symptom: A Lessons Learnt run stalls or the deck looks wrong
steps: Check the run's status and which of the fourteen stages last saved.
Rerun the offline render script to see if the deck builds without the database.
Compare with the routing dry run if themes look misplaced.

debug_playbook.symptom: An import changed data unexpectedly or shows gaps
steps: Rerun the import as a dry run first.
Run verify.ts to see which suite fails.
Run the scan evidence check to list projects lacking sourced values.

glossary.meaning: The app's shared database of projects, evidence and saved run records.
A benchmark tool comparing planned and actual budgets and schedule delays across projects.
A tool that groups evidence into themes (pillars) explaining why projects succeeded or struggled, and builds a slide deck.
A tool that captures signals about new capital projects and ranks them into priority tiers.
An exact passage from a web page or PDF that backs a stored fact.
A check that a quoted passage really appears in the cited document.
Batches of researched replies that add new projects or fill gaps in existing ones.
A list of approved research batches that can be loaded into another database in order.
Measurement checks: E14 tests whether scoring criteria separate overrun projects from on-time ones, and E25 checks that numbers can be traced to sources.
Running an import or script to show what would change without saving anything.
